value: A screen was judged from one render at a comfortable width; at the real narrow pane times wrapped (12:30 P/M) and cards truncated (3 recor…), and the owner found it. Rule: every UI scene gets a 380pt twin with long titles and long errors, and the PNGs are READ before the change is called done; lineLimit(1) on a reason hides it, so let reasons wrap.

A hexa loop task was marked done that was never built (notes search), and another was done by mistake. Rule: hexa loop task done only for work with a commit; at the end of work compare hexa loop with git log and undo the rest.

Dictation and Notes were merged (dictation wrote a copy into Notes) before the owner had separated three functions. Rule: Recordings (meetings), Notes (in-app Record button, text kept), Dictation (types into the app in front, keeps nothing) share no data; ask which function a request belongs to before wiring anything between them.

Ad-hoc codesign identifies the app by binary hash, so every rebuild lost the Accessibility grant; toggling the switch does not replace the saved requirement. Rule: sign with designated => identifier com.gaberger.earshot, diagnose with the tccd log (log show), fix with tccutil reset Accessibility, and do not call it fixed until it survives a rebuild.

ImageRenderer draws native controls as yellow boxes, an offscreen window shows switches grey (not key), and render.sh deletes the PNGs first. Rule: render through an offscreen NSWindow, ignore grey switches, and never run render.sh while an agent is reading /tmp/earshot-ui.

Two sessions work in one working tree and leave untracked ADRs and folders; a blanket git add -A would commit the other's work, and build.sh changed under me (it now globs *.swift). Rule: git status first, git add only your own paths, read a file again before editing it, and use *.swift in typecheck evidence.

The first wrong-window guard compared window frames; two maximized windows of one app, and tabs or panes in one window, share a frame, so it pasted anyway. CFHash of an AXUIElement turned out to be pid plus a constant, so it cannot tell windows apart. Rule: identify a target by the element itself (CFEqual on the focused window and focused element), keep geometry only as a fallback, log the decision inputs (never the text), and say plainly which part could not be tested without Accessibility.
